newsitem.title: UK: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - July 11.
newsitem.headline: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - July 11.

text.p: ....REUTERS WORLDWIDE ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST.....
Reuters news from around the world on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends ***********************************************
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

WINSTON-SALEM, North Carolina - The RJ Reynolds Tobacco Co., bowing to pressure from tobacco critics, including President Bill Clinton, says it is retiring its controversial Joe Camel advertising character.

LONDON - Drinks and retailing group Allied Domecq Plc says it will pioneer the use of "virtual" television advertising in Britain. It will use new technology to place electronically "virtual" perimeter board advertising for four of its spirits brands on Sky Sports live coverage of the England Vs Australia rugby game.

FRANKFURT The right marketing strategy is increasingly making the difference between success or failure for financial services, participants at a conference say. Industry experts say financial services ads must have an emotional pull.
DUSSELDORF - Advertising group Euro RSCG says it plans to consolidate its business in Germany into two agencies: Euro RSCG Werbeagentur and Euro RSCG Thomsen.
LONDON - Ad agency DDB's Moroccan affiliate Zone Bleue has won the Mobil account in Morocco. The DDB network now runs the Mobil account in over 40 countries.

DREIEICH, Germany - German insurance company Axa Direkt says it plans to invest up to 10 million marks ($5.7 million) in a new print and television advertising campaign featuring popular comic book character Asterix.
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

NEW YORK - Westinghouse Electric Corp's CBS Inc unit disputes the findings of a study by the cable television industry that basic cable networks grabbed as many viewers as the broadcast networks have lost this year.
WASHINGTON - Vice President Al Gore hails a voluntary agreement by major U.S. television networks to add a content rating coding system to their programmes.

BONN - A dozen top companies in the German multimedia industry say they have formed their own watchdog organisation to keep their Internet services free of content considered indecent or illegal. The new group includes Microsoft, ProSieben Media and Deutsche Telekom.
TOKYO - Discovery Japan Inc says it has launched a 24-hour non-fiction entertainment broadcasting network in Japan.
NEW YORK - Newspaper companies, boosted by a healthy U.S. economy that has propelled strong advertising growth, are expected to post profit gains as high as 35 percent in the second quarter.

SEATTLE - Sales continued to soar in the latest quarter at Internet bookseller Amazon.com Inc. but losses deepened, the company says in its first earnings report since going public in May. The Seattle-based Internet start-up lost $6.7 million, or 28 cents per share, in the second quarter ended June 30. Sales soared to $27.9 million.

SOFIA - Bulgaria's parliament has replaced directors of state media appointed under the former Socialist government, state radio says. Deputies voted to replace Milen Valkov as director of state news agency BTA with Panayot Denev, a longstanding employee of the agency, the radio says.
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

PARIS - Lancome, a subsidiary of French cosmetics group L'Oreal, will for the first time launch a new product simultaneously in several markets around the world, designed to build product awareness among women who are increasingly travelling more. The new skincare product, a night cream called Primordiale Nuit, will be launched in Europe, the U.S. and Japan in September.
TOKYO - Toyota Motor Corp says it will set up a project team to develop vehicles targeting a younger market, as it seeks to shore up its domestic market share.

LONDON - British drinks manufacturer Merrydown Plc says annual profits were undermined by a decline in the sale of its Two Dogs brand, one of the so called "alcopops", which has caused controversy in recent months over under-age drinking.

LOS ANGELES - U.S. album sales rose 5.4 percent in the first half of 1997, marking a turnaround for the $12 billion music industry, whose sales have been flat for the past two years, industry experts say.

SHANGHAI - Shanghai General Automobile Sales Co has cut the price of the Santana 2000 sedan, made by a joint venture with Germany's Volkswagen, for the second time this year to deal with fierce competition in the market, the China Business Daily says.
CONSUMER TRENDS:

PARIS - French kids prefer Kinder chocolate eggs and pocket-sized cakes to Coca-Cola, according to a recent study into French children's brand preferences by research institute L'Institut de l'Enfant.
HANOI - Vietnam, one of the world's poorest countries where ownership of a water buffalo is still considered a rural status symbol, says mobile phone usage is soaring.
LONDON - Job seekers who take part in group therapy are three times more likely to get jobs than those who just try networking, British psychologists report.

SOFIA - Bulgaria's population is expected to fall by one million to about seven million by 2020 as a low birth rate, economic crisis and high emigration take their toll, the National Statistics Institute says.
